title: Matched minority public-opponent hero learned-weight smoke
benchmark: A frozen learned policy plays at least 100,000 fresh 200bb HUNL Slumbot hands, scores above 0 bb/100, and has a 95% confidence-interval lower bound above 0.
hypothesis: Replacing 25% of external-opponent hands (18.75% overall at 25% self-play) with the frozen public Slumbot behavior model will add opponent-conditioned reward signal without reviving hero imitation, yielding a broader frozen greedy policy than an otherwise identical Standard10-initialized diverse learned-league control.
material_change: Train matched 8,192-physical-hand control and treatment from frozen Standard10 with identical PPO, fixed learned opponents, self-play share, worker/deal seeds, and source KL. Treatment alone activates the frozen public opponent at 0.25 of external hands. Freeze endpoints and compare on untouched common-deck learned-policy anchors.
baseline: Standard10 is the reproducible frontier parent. Historical single imitation was -18.5025 fresh20k. Public model is opponent-only, session-disjoint, and worker-contract qualified; Standard10 exploited it at +97.7959 internally, so its share is capped.

notes: No Slumbot network calls. Public-history outcomes are not training labels. Treatment fraction and all promotion gates fixed before training.

Untouched production gate fixed before evaluation: 2,048 common-deck mirrored pairs per candidate per each of four legacy-v4 learned anchors (32,768 hands total). Promote only if treatment-minus-control point estimate is positive on at least 3/4 anchors, pooled paired delta is positive, Standard10 delta is nonnegative, and pooled seat-0 and seat-1 deltas are each nonnegative. Confidence intervals are reported diagnostically; this smoke is not a Slumbot milestone.

result.summary: Matched Standard10-initialized PPO smoke completed after two rejected infrastructure attempts preserved in place. Accepted control and treatment each completed two updates; treatment saw 2,281 public-opponent hands and 4,557 bypassed decisions across all 12 workers. Untouched four-anchor common-deck evaluation covered 32,768 hands.
result.conclusion: The public Slumbot opponent model is behaviorally learnable and executable, but adding it as a 25% external-opponent minority member harmed general learned-anchor performance. Treatment-control deltas were negative on all four anchors; pooled paired delta was -9.9883 bb/100 with 95% CI [-19.6636,-0.3130]. Raw evidence, frozen hashes, accounting, and 12-worker audit all passed.
result.next_step: Retain the matched control as the only candidate from this experiment. Do not scale public-opponent mixture or revisit imitation. Compare the control against relevant prior Standard10-preserving PPO results and select the highest-information independent confirmation or fresh Slumbot gate.
